test_title: PYST 52: SSC CPO - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A dealer sells his goods at 10% loss on the cost price but uses 25% less weight. What is his profit percentage?
solution:
Given:

Sell goods = CP — 10%

False weight in selling = 25% less

Concept:

Percentage profit = Profit / CP × 100

Profit = SP —CP

Cost price + Profit% = Selling price

Selling price — Profit = Cost price

Market price — Discount = Selling price

Calculation:

Let cost price = 100

Percentage loss = 10% ⇒ 10

Selling price = 100 — 10 ⇒ 90

Uses less weight = 25%

⇒ 25% × 100

⇒ 25

Actual cost price = 100 — 25

⇒ 75

CP = 75

SP = 90

Percentage profit = (SP — CP)/CP × 100

⇒ (90 — 75)/75 × 100

⇒ 15/75 × 100

⇒ 20%

∴ The actual gain or loss percentage is 20%.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] Alternate Method__

Profit% or loss% = (%less weight — %loss)/ (100 — %less weight) × 100

⇒ (25 — 10)/ (100 — 25) × 100

⇒ 15/75 × 100

⇒ 20%

∴ The actual gain or loss percentage is 20%.
